why: tip_tongue adds a blade that slides 0.3-5 cm behind the teeth and seals the full bore, which gives /t/. Setting the body pad's stroke to 1.3 lets it seal at the velar place for /k/, with 0.1 cm of margin against servo noise. The second constriction might also help /ɝ/ (F3 needs constrictions at two places at once), but I am not counting on it. Cost: a $4 pushrod kit plus one $8 servo (4 servos needed, 2 reused, 1 on hand), so $12, 3 days, 76 machine minutes. Combined with round_lips: 6 servos (2 more bought), 6 of 6 channels, about $24 in total.

round_lips opens from 0 to 6.6 cm2, which gives a full lip seal for /p/ while the tongue keeps the rest of the airway open (> 0.2 cm2). A small rounded opening plus up to 1.6 cm of protrusion (lip tube up to 2.6 cm, effective tract about 16 cm instead of 14.5) should pull F2 down to /u/ and /ʊ/ levels with a back tongue constriction, and /ɔ/ down with moderate rounding. Rounding also lowers F1, which helps uw (F1 +43%) and uh (+14%). Cost: $4 for a pushrod kit, 2 days, 57 machine minutes. The second lip servo is the one on hand.
